intent: Authenticated customer disputes a £4,980 Direct Debit collected on 14 Sep by Lime Property via H&V Collect (he says the move-in money was already paid by Faster Payment on 28 Aug and the agreed rent is £795), wants a full refund today under the Direct Debit Guarantee and wants the mandate cancelled.
summary: Raise a Direct Debit Guarantee claim for the 14 Sep £4,980 collection with the DD disputes team (passing the 28 Aug FP of the same amount, 2 Sep mandate, 9 Sep advance notice that matched the collection) and ask for the unarranged overdraft fees to be reviewed with it; propose cancellation of mandate LP-14GROVE-0208 as instructed; ask the customer for tenancy/move-in paperwork showing agreed amounts; reply that both actions are pending, no same-day refund is promised, and he should also raise the apparent double charge with Lime Property.

facts.claim: Customer passed ID&V on the phone channel and is the account holder (Tunde Okoye, personal current account).
A Faster Payment of £4,980.00 to HARROW & VALE RE LIME PROPERTY CA, reference MOVE IN 14 GROVE, completed on 28 Aug 2026; the bank record does not show how the agency allocated it.
A DD mandate H&V COLLECT / LIME PROPERTY (LP-14GROVE-0208) was created on 2 Sep 2026 via originator invite.

An advance notice dated 9 Sep 2026 (originator copy) stated a first collection of £4,980.00 on 14 Sep 2026 described as 'balance of your account as at 8 September', then £795.00 monthly on the 14th, and told the customer to contact Lime Property before the collection date if any amount was incorrect. The customer says he did not read it.
On 14 Sep 2026 a DD collection of £4,980.00 was paid, taking the balance to -£3,077.70; an unarranged overdraft daily fee of £6.50 was then charged (balance -£3,084.20). Arranged limit is £1,000.

Customer asserts the monthly rent is £795, that he paid all move-in money by bank transfer, and that he never agreed to £4,980 by Direct Debit; he wants a full refund today under the Guarantee and the mandate cancelled.
The collected amount and date match the advance notice; whether the amount itself was an error by the originator is a disputed point not resolved by the supplied records.

missing: The customer's tenancy/move-in paperwork showing the agreed move-in sum and monthly rent (to evidence that £4,980 was not owed again).
How Lime Property allocated the 28 Aug £4,980 Faster Payment (bank record does not show this).
Confirmation of how the mandate was completed on 2 Sep (customer's own acceptance of the originator invite) and what amount, if any, he agreed at setup.
The bank's internal Direct Debit indemnity claim procedure and its criteria/timescales (not supplied).
The bank's policy on refunding unarranged overdraft fees arising from a disputed collection (not supplied).

steps.instruction: Ask the Direct Debit disputes/indemnity team to assess a Direct Debit Guarantee claim for the 14 Sep 2026 collection of £4,980.00, H&V COLLECT / LIME PROPERTY, reference LP-14GROVE-0208, on Tunde Okoye's personal current account (SYN-ACCT-15-1). Pass: customer disputes the amount (states agreed rent is £795 and all move-in money was already paid); 28 Aug 2026 Faster Payment HV26082811320471 of £4,980.00 to HARROW & VALE RE LIME PROPERTY CA ref MOVE IN 14 GROVE (completed; allocation by agency not shown in bank record); mandate created 2 Sep via originator invite; 9 Sep advance notice stated £4,980.00 on 14 Sep then £795 monthly, and the collection matched it; customer says he did not read the notice. Ask the team to determine whether this is treated as an indemnity claim or referred to the originator, and to review the unarranged overdraft daily fees (£6.50/day from 14 Sep, balance -£3,084.20 against £1,000 arranged limit) as a consequence of the disputed collection. Customer paperwork from s3 to follow.

rationale.explanation: The customer has made a Guarantee claim; the supplied records show the collection matched the advance notice but the customer asserts the amount was never agreed and the same sum was already paid by transfer, so the error question needs assessment under the bank's process rather than an immediate refund promise.
rationale.criterion: Identify the alleged error and the applicable route for a Direct Debit Guarantee claim without promising a refund for every dispute with a supplier; keep the claim separate from changing future instructions.

steps.target: Direct Debit disputes / indemnity team (Harrow & Vale Bank plc)

steps.instruction: Ask the payments servicing team to cancel Direct Debit instruction LP-14GROVE-0208 (H&V COLLECT / LIME PROPERTY) on Tunde Okoye's personal current account on the customer's authenticated instruction given by phone on 14 Sep 2026. Record that the customer was told the next scheduled collection (£795 on 14 Oct) will not be taken once cancelled and that cancellation does not reverse the 14 Sep collection.

rationale.explanation: The ID&V-passed account holder explicitly instructed cancellation of the mandate; this is a supported change and is independent of the Guarantee claim.
rationale.criterion: Cancel the instruction on the customer's authority; cancelling an instruction does not establish that a collected payment was reversed or a contract ended.

steps.target: Payments servicing team (Harrow & Vale Bank plc)

steps.instruction: Ask Tunde Okoye to send a copy of his tenancy agreement or Lime Property move-in statement/invoice showing the agreed move-in sum and the monthly rent of £795, so it can be attached to the Guarantee claim as evidence that the £4,980 collected on 14 Sep was not an amount he agreed to pay by Direct Debit.

rationale.explanation: The bank's records show the collection matched the advance notice; the customer's assertion that the amount was not owed needs supporting documentation of the agreed amounts for the claim assessment.
rationale.criterion: If a gap changes the decision, name the precise missing fact and a concrete request to obtain it.

steps.instruction: Tell the customer: 'I've raised a Direct Debit Guarantee claim for the £4,980 collected today by Lime Property via H&V Collect (reference LP-14GROVE-0208) with our Direct Debit disputes team. I have to be straight with you: the amount and date taken match the advance notice sent on 9 September, so the team will need to assess whether this counts as an error under the Guarantee — I can't promise the money back today, and nothing has been refunded yet. I've recorded that you never agreed to £4,980 by Direct Debit and that you paid £4,980 by transfer on 28 August (ref MOVE IN 14 GROVE). To support the claim, please send a copy of your tenancy agreement or move-in invoice showing the agreed amounts. I've also requested cancellation of the Direct Debit as you asked; that isn't confirmed yet, and once it is, no further collections will be taken — including the £795 due on 14 October — so you'll need to pay rent another way. Cancelling doesn't reverse today's collection or change what the agency says you owe. Separately, please contact Lime Property now about the apparent double payment and ask them to refund it or explain how they allocated your 28 August transfer. Your account is in unarranged overdraft and a £6.50 daily fee is being charged; I've asked for those fees to be reviewed with the claim, but no waiver is confirmed. If the overdraft leaves you unable to cover essentials, tell us and we can refer you to our financial support team. If you're unhappy with how we handle this, you can make a complaint to us and, after our response, to the Financial Ombudsman Service.'

rationale.explanation: The customer needs an accurate status: claim and cancellation raised but pending, no refund promised, what cancellation does and does not do, the fee position, and the direct route with the agency.
rationale.criterion: Reply with the recorded status and what it does not confirm; a request to change is not a confirmed change and a review request does not establish a refund.

must_state: The Guarantee claim for the 14 Sep £4,980 collection has been raised for assessment by the bank's Direct Debit disputes team; it is not yet decided and no refund has been made.
The collection matched the advance notice sent on 9 Sep, which is relevant to how the claim is assessed; the customer's position that the amount was never agreed has been recorded.

Cancellation of mandate LP-14GROVE-0208 has been requested but is not yet confirmed; once cancelled no further collections (including the £795 due 14 Oct) will be taken, so rent must be paid another way; cancelling does not reverse the 14 Sep collection or change what he owes the agency.
He should also contact Lime Property directly about the apparent double payment (28 Aug transfer plus 14 Sep collection) and ask for a refund or written explanation of the allocation.
The account is in unarranged overdraft and a £6.50 daily fee is being charged; a review of those fees has been requested alongside the claim but no waiver is confirmed.
If he is dissatisfied with the bank's handling or outcome he can raise a complaint with the bank and, after that, with the Financial Ombudsman Service.
must_not: Do not promise a refund today or state that the Guarantee automatically entitles him to a refund of this collection.
Do not state that the collection was, or was not, an error by the originator or the bank.
Do not say the Direct Debit has already been cancelled or that fees have been waived.
Do not suggest the 28 Aug Faster Payment can be recalled or was refunded.
Do not imply cancelling the mandate ends his tenancy obligations or the agency's claim to any money.
Do not give a fixed complaint response deadline or predict an Ombudsman outcome.
